sentences.text: Lindwurmia thiuda is the sole species of a small rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur that lived in Germany during the Early Jurassic. This animal measured between 2 and 3 meters in length, with fully grown individuals reaching approximately 3 meters.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in 1899 by Johannes Maak in a clay quarry in Halberstadt, Germany. It consists of an incomplete skeleton including sixty-nine vertebrae, jaw fragments, and partial limb girdles. Theodore Brandes first described the specimen in 1912 and 1914, but Peggy Vincent and Glenn William Storrs formally named the species Lindwurmia thiuda in 2019.
Research by Vincent and Storrs in 2019 classified Lindwurmia as the sister taxon to Anningasaura within the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Lindwurmia lived during the Hettangian stage, approximately 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
